screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind trial comparing aminophylline (theophylline analogue) with placebo in patients with acute ischaemic stroke. Likely randomised, treatment started during acute phase (3-day infusion). Meets all selection criteria.

Double-blind RCT of intravenous aminophylline vs placebo in 79 patients with acute cerebral infarction. Treatment started within the acute phase, fulfilling population, intervention, comparator, and design requirements.
Open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation study without a concurrent placebo or control group. Not a randomised trial; does not meet study design criterion.

Study investigates vincamin (not a theophylline analogue) and does not compare theophylline/analogue to placebo/control. Participants are not clearly acute ischaemic stroke patients. Fails population, intervention, and design criteria.

Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over trial of caffeine (an analogue) in patients recovering from acute ischaemic stroke. While timing of treatment relative to stroke onset is unclear, conservative inclusion is warranted.

Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over trial of caffeine in stroke patients. Similar to Study 5; conservative inclusion as it may fall within the spectrum of acute ischaemic stroke and meets the intervention/comparator design.
Not a randomised trial. Intracarotid aminophylline infusion study without a placebo or control group. Does not meet the required comparative design.
Animal experiment (cats with middle cerebral artery occlusion). Not a human study, thus fails the population criterion.

Animal experiment (anesthetized dogs). Not a trial in patients with acute ischaemic stroke, and does not compare a theophylline analogue against placebo/control. Excluded on population and design grounds.
Appears to be a narrative review discussing historical studies; no original trial data. Not a randomised controlled trial. Excluded due to study design.
